title: P201516142
treatment_protocol_ch1: These are baseline bladder tissue results prior to any chemotherapy being received by the patients in the clinical trial
extract_protocol_ch1: All FFPE tissues were first de-paraffinized with a xylene followed by ethanol dehydration. Tissue samples were then disrupted during an optimised overnight incubation with a Proteinase K. Nucleic acids were bound to a glass fibre filter in the presence of a chaotropic salt under conditions that were optimized specifically for RNA & miRNA recovery. Bound RNA was subjected to a series of wash steps to remove contaminating cellular components, and any residual DNA was digested by incubation with DNaseI followed by further wash steps to improve the final purity of the RNA, which was then eluted from the glass fibres in a small volume of water.
hyb_protocol: Labelled cDNA was combined with dimethyl sulfoxide, hybridization buffer and nuclease free water and hybridised onto a HG-U133_Plus_2 Array (ThermoFisher) for 18hrs at 40oC.  Following hybridization, all arrays were washed using buffers of varying salt concentrations and stained with streptavidin-phycoerythrin conjugate (SAPE) .    All reaction components are contained within the hybridization, wash and stain kit (ThermoFisher).
scan_protocol: The arrays were scanned on the GeneChip scanner system (Thermofisher) using an epiflourescent, confocal microscope.  A solid-state laser contained within the GeneChip system was used to excite fluorophores bound to the hybridized cDNA molecules. The fluorescent values were firstly converted into an electronic signal and then to a numerical value representing the fluorescent intensity.
data_processing: CEL file intensities have been normalised to probeset level using Robust Multichip Average (RMA) consisting background adjustment, quantile normalisation and summarisation pre-processing (Bolstad et al, 2003).

Nucleic acids were bound to a glass fibre filter in the presence of a chaotropic salt under conditions that were optimized specifically for RNA & miRNA recovery. Bound RNA was subjected to a series of wash steps to remove contaminating cellular components, and any residual DNA was digested by incubation with DNaseI followed by further wash steps to improve the final purity of the RNA, which was then eluted from the glass fibres in a small volume of water.
hyb_protocol: Labelled cDNA was combined with dimethyl sulfoxide, hybridization buffer and nuclease free water and hybridised onto a HG-U133_Plus_2 Array (ThermoFisher) for 18hrs at 40oC.  Following hybridization, all arrays were washed using buffers of varying salt concentrations and stained with streptavidin-phycoerythrin conjugate (SAPE) .    All reaction components are contained within the hybridization, wash and stain kit (ThermoFisher).
scan_protocol: The arrays were scanned on the GeneChip scanner system (Thermofisher) using an epiflourescent, confocal microscope.  A solid-state laser contained within the GeneChip system was used to excite fluorophores bound to the hybridized cDNA molecules. The fluorescent values were firstly converted into an electronic signal and then to a numerical value representing the fluorescent intensity.
data_processing: CEL file intensities have been normalised to probeset level using Robust Multichip Average (RMA) consisting background adjustment, quantile normalisation and summarisation pre-processing (Bolstad et al, 2003).

extract_protocol_ch1: All FFPE tissues were first de-paraffinized with a xylene followed by ethanol dehydration. Tissue samples were then disrupted during an optimised overnight incubation with a Proteinase K. Nucleic acids were bound to a glass fibre filter in the presence of a chaotropic salt under conditions that were optimized specifically for RNA & miRNA recovery. Bound RNA was subjected to a series of wash steps to remove contaminating cellular components, and any residual DNA was digested by incubation with DNaseI followed by further wash steps to improve the final purity of the RNA, which was then eluted from the glass fibres in a small volume of water.
hyb_protocol: Labelled cDNA was combined with dimethyl sulfoxide, hybridization buffer and nuclease free water and hybridised onto a HG-U133_Plus_2 Array (ThermoFisher) for 18hrs at 40oC.  Following hybridization, all arrays were washed using buffers of varying salt concentrations and stained with streptavidin-phycoerythrin conjugate (SAPE) .    All reaction components are contained within the hybridization, wash and stain kit (ThermoFisher).
scan_protocol: The arrays were scanned on the GeneChip scanner system (Thermofisher) using an epiflourescent, confocal microscope.  A solid-state laser contained within the GeneChip system was used to excite fluorophores bound to the hybridized cDNA molecules. The fluorescent values were firstly converted into an electronic signal and then to a numerical value representing the fluorescent intensity.
data_processing: CEL file intensities have been normalised to probeset level using Robust Multichip Average (RMA) consisting background adjustment, quantile normalisation and summarisation pre-processing (Bolstad et al, 2003).
